newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for June 27.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for June 27.

text.p: All Mexican ports were open on Friday, as Tropical Storm Carlos was reduced to a depression off the Pacific Coast, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1500 local/2000 GMT daily meteorological report.
Tropical Depression Carlos was spotted Friday afternoon at approximately 130 miles northwest of Clarion island off the Pacific coast, moving west at approximately 10 knots (19 km/11 miles).
Carlos showered rains on the Revillagigedo islands, about 600 km/375 miles west of Mexico's Pacific coast.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Pacific Coast, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean.
Tropical Depression Carlos dropping light rain along the coast with maximum winds 10 to 20 knots (19 to 38 km/11 to 22 miles per hour) and waves three to seven feet high.

Light to medium rains expected later in the day along coasts of Veracruz, Tabasco and Campeche states. Generally clear skies and maximum winds from 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 16 miles per hour) and waves three to six feet high.
Rainy and cloudy in region with some thunder storms. Winds from 10 to 15 knots and from three to six feet.

Two storm fronts were spotted in the region, one off the coast of Panama moving west at 10 to 15 knots and the other off the coast of Colombia, moving west at between 15 and 20 knots (28 to 38 km/16 to 22 miles).
